layout.children: children/<name>/ (each an independently portable events.jsonl with its own ancillary run.json)
layout.discovery: events.jsonl is self-describing: its declaration records carry the format, schema, run context, contracts, sources, definitions, children, source ends and finalization; a reader given events.jsonl needs nothing else; this run.json is an ancillary index and summary and may be absent

reader_compat.note: reader/software compatibility is pinned separately from the OCSF version, the extension version, the mapping contract versions and this package layout version

persisted_prefix.meaning: sha256 of the first `bytes` bytes of events.jsonl as persisted at the last flush (declaration and event lines); a reader of an open package can verify this prefix

acquisition.meaning: complete: every declared source ended by EOF with its last record whole; this is relative to the declared sources and does not prove the vendor produced nothing else

recording.durability: flush(): buffered event bytes are written to events.jsonl and run.json is replaced atomically (rename); they are then visible to other processes on this host through the OS page cache. fsync (FileChannel.force) is requested only at finalization and on failure, before the final hash is computed from the file as it is on disk. Nothing is claimed about power loss between a flush and finalization.

cli.name: Claude Code
cli.version_basis: declared by the capture at launch

qualification.basis: exact native version/session and original-byte extent checks; canonical verification is separate

launch_settings.acquired_execution_basis: caller-supplied immutable acquisition manifest; not a vendor assertion

children.basis: records whose owner path (parent_tool_use_id) equals the spawning tool call id, routed by the mapper as they arrived (labelled split; not live child support)

source_scope.basis: this core owns the records of the artifact whose owner_path member equals owner_value (null: records without one); a tool_progress record names the tool call in progress in parent_tool_use_id and is owned here (claude.stream.progress_owner.v1)

ocsf.compiled_schema_location: referenced by hash; the definitions this core needs are declared in events.jsonl before use

extension.name: agentic_cli
extension.reader_rule: resolve class names through this pin; refuse a package whose pinned uid/class table differs from the reader's compiled schema

definitions.kind: declared in events.jsonl (definition records, before use) + extension-source here

categories.json.caption: Categories
categories.json.description: Categories added by the Agentic CLI extension.
categories.json.name: category

agent_execution.caption: Agent Execution
agent_execution.description: Observed execution of an agentic CLI: prompt turns, model responses, tool calls and their operations, and retained native source records.

dictionary.json.caption: Attribute Dictionary
dictionary.json.description: Attributes added by the Agentic CLI extension. Core attributes (data, raw_data, exit_code, name, version, product, status_id, time) are reused where their core definition fits.
dictionary.json.name: dictionary

cli_agent.caption: CLI Agent
cli_agent.description: The agentic CLI that produced the observed execution, as this extension's cli_agent object.

journal.caption: Journal Provenance
journal.description: Agent Journal's own provenance for this event: run and invocation identity, producer, mapping contract, capture time and sequence. Distinct from metadata.product, which names the originating CLI.

source_ref.caption: Source Reference
source_ref.description: Which native source artifact and record occurrence supplied the facts in this event or object.

session_uid.caption: Session ID
session_uid.description: The native session identifier reported by the CLI (ACP session). Not a Journal run identifier.

turn_uid.caption: Prompt Turn ID
turn_uid.description: The native identifier of the prompt turn, when the source reports one.

run_uid.caption: Journal Run ID
run_uid.description: The Agent Journal run identifier that owns this event.

invocation_index.caption: Invocation Index
invocation_index.description: Zero-based index of the CLI invocation within the Journal run.

response_uid.caption: Model Response ID
response_uid.description: The model provider's identifier of the model response (for example the Anthropic message id), when the source reports one. Never a source-local item identifier, and absent when no response identifier is reported.

tool_call_uid.caption: Tool Call ID
tool_call_uid.description: The native identifier of the tool call request. Absent when the source does not report one for the record.

tool_name.caption: Tool Name
tool_name.description: The exact tool name as the source reports it. Never normalized, and absent when the source reports no name: a family or item type (tool_family) is not a name.

tool_kind_id.caption: Tool Kind ID
tool_kind_id.description: The ACP tool kind of the requested tool activity, assigned by a declared mapping rule named in tool_kind_basis. A kind describes the request; it is not evidence of an operating-system effect.

tool_kind.caption: Tool Kind
tool_kind.description: The ACP tool kind caption, sibling of tool_kind_id.

tool_kind_basis.caption: Tool Kind Basis
tool_kind_basis.description: The declared mapping rule that assigned tool_kind_id: a table over tool names the source reports for its own tools, a table over source families, or a reviewed namespace binding. A name under another namespace (for example an MCP tool named like a built-in tool) never takes the built-in's kind. Shell command parsing is not a permitted basis.

arguments.caption: Tool Arguments
arguments.description: The tool request arguments exactly as the source reported them (object, string or other JSON value).

content_blocks.caption: Content Blocks
content_blocks.description: Ordered content blocks of a message as reported by the source.

block_index.caption: Block Index
block_index.description: Zero-based position of the block within the source record's content array.

block_type.caption: Block Type
block_type.description: The native block type string, exactly as reported.

block_kind_id.caption: Block Kind ID
block_kind_id.description: ACP-style content kind of the block, assigned by a declared mapping rule.

text.caption: Text
text.description: The text content of a block when the source reports text.

tool_result.caption: Tool Result
tool_result.description: The observed result of a tool call as the source returned it.

error_reported.caption: Error Reported
error_reported.description: Whether the source explicitly flagged the result as an error. Absent when the source reports nothing.

structured_result.caption: Structured Result
structured_result.description: Structured result detail the CLI reported beside the model-visible content (for example Claude's tool_use_result).

argv.caption: Command Vector
argv.description: The command as an argument vector when the source reports it that way.

reported_state.caption: Reported State
reported_state.description: The lifecycle state string exactly as the source reported it (for example DONE, completed, failed).

attribution.caption: Attribution
attribution.description: How this fact was associated with its owner, with the declared outcome, candidates and basis.

outcome_id.caption: Attribution Outcome ID
outcome_id.description: Whether the owner of a fact could be established from the source.

1.caption: Unique
1.description: Exactly one owner is established by the declared join keys.

2.caption: Ambiguous
2.description: More than one candidate owner satisfies the declared join keys; the fact is attached at the enclosing scope only.

3.caption: Unattributed
3.description: The source provides no key to any owner; the fact is retained at its reported scope.

candidates.caption: Candidate Owners
candidates.description: Identifiers of the candidate owners considered.

basis.caption: Basis
basis.description: The declared rule, join keys or reason behind a classification, derivation or fallback.

scope_uid.caption: Scope ID
scope_uid.description: Identifier of the scope within which candidates were considered (for example a turn id).

permission_decision.caption: Permission Decision
permission_decision.description: A permission decision reported by the source at its reported scope.

permission_decisions.caption: Permission Decisions
permission_decisions.description: Permission decisions reported at the scope of this event.

decision_id.caption: Decision ID
decision_id.description: Normalized permission decision. The core sibling decision carries the caption; reported_decision carries the source's own label.

decision_source.caption: Decision Source
decision_source.description: Who or what made the decision, as reported (for example config, user, cli).

reason_type.caption: Reason Type
reason_type.description: The reason category reported with the decision.

scope_id.caption: Scope ID
scope_id.description: The scope at which the source reported this observation. 99 Other names, in its sibling scope, a unit the source defines that no other value describes.

7.caption: Child run
7.description: The run of a sub-agent that a tool call spawned. Where the unit is identified depends on the object (see usage_observation); its observations are never added to the parent's or the run's totals.

99.caption: Other
99.description: A unit the source itself defines, which none of the other scopes describes; the sibling scope names it (for example Conversation step). It is not established to be the unit of any other scope (a conversation step is not stated to be one model response), and units of different source artifacts are never joined by equal identifiers. Where the unit is identified depends on the object (see usage_observation).

8.caption: Agent
8.description: An explicitly reported agent subject identified by the enclosing event reported_agent, scoped to its source artifact and run. Main agent is not a spawned child; no parent/spawn relationship is implied.

scope.caption: Scope
scope.description: Caption sibling of scope_id; for 99 Other, the name of the source-defined unit.

usage_observations.caption: Usage Observations
usage_observations.description: Reported token usage observations, each tied to its source record, scope and provisional/final status. Several may exist for one response; they are never reconciled into one value.

usage_status_id.caption: Usage Status ID
usage_status_id.description: Whether the reported usage is provisional or final, as established by the declared rule in basis.

output_tokens.caption: Output Tokens
output_tokens.description: Output tokens as the source reports them. When reasoning_relation_id is 1, reasoning_tokens are part of this count, never in addition to it.

cache_read_tokens.caption: Cache Read Tokens
cache_read_tokens.description: Input tokens read from a prompt cache. Disjoint from uncached_input_tokens and cache_write_tokens.

cache_write_tokens.caption: Cache Write Tokens
cache_write_tokens.description: Input tokens written to a prompt cache, every retention or pricing tier together. Disjoint from uncached_input_tokens and cache_read_tokens; cache_write_tiers breaks it down without adding to it.

reasoning_tokens.caption: Reasoning Tokens
reasoning_tokens.description: Reasoning or thinking output tokens as the source reports them. reasoning_relation_id states whether they are part of output_tokens; absent there, the relation is not established and they must not be added to or subtracted from output_tokens.

reported_total_tokens.caption: Reported Total Tokens
reported_total_tokens.description: A total token figure only when the source reported it as a total. Never computed.

cost_observation.caption: Cost Observation
cost_observation.description: A reported cost, stored as a total with its scope, basis and source.

total_cost.caption: Total Cost
total_cost.description: The reported cost total exactly as reported.

currency.caption: Currency
currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code of the reported cost.

cost_basis.caption: Cost Basis
cost_basis.description: The source's reported pricing basis, if any (for example list).

model_ref.caption: Model Reference
model_ref.description: Minimal reported-model reference. Used instead of core ai_model when the source does not report a provider organization.

provider_kind.caption: Provider Kind
provider_kind.description: A provider classification the source reported (for example firstParty). Not an organization name.

provider_basis_id.caption: Provider Basis ID
provider_basis_id.description: Whether provider information was reported, derived or is unavailable.

stop_reason.caption: Stop Reason
stop_reason.description: The stop reason string exactly as the source reported it.

status_basis_id.caption: Status Basis ID
status_basis_id.description: Whether status_id was reported by the source, derived by a declared Journal rule, or could not be derived.

derivation.caption: Derivation
derivation.description: Identifier of the declared rule and inputs used to derive a value.

time_basis_id.caption: Time Basis ID
time_basis_id.description: How the event's time was established.

1.caption: Source record
1.description: The source record reports a timestamp; time is that value and metadata.original_time holds its text.

2.caption: Earliest available fallback
2.description: The record reports no time; time is the latest preceding source-reported time in the same occurrence sequence, or the capture start when none precedes. basis names which.

3.caption: Capture observation
3.description: The event is a Journal observation; time is when Journal observed it.

source_kind_id.caption: Source Kind ID
source_kind_id.description: What kind of artifact supplied the fact: the CLI's live output (standard output or standard error), a native session file it saved, a telemetry export it wrote (native OTel), a report file it wrote at exit, or its own log file.

3.caption: Telemetry export
3.description: A telemetry file the CLI's own exporter wrote during the run (for example the OTel file exporter).

4.caption: CLI report file
4.description: A report the CLI wrote at the end of the run (for example a usage report file).

5.caption: CLI log file
5.description: The CLI's own diagnostic log, or a declared excerpt of it.

artifact.caption: Artifact
artifact.description: Name of the source artifact within the run's source inventory.

artifact_sha256.caption: Artifact SHA-256
artifact_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the complete source artifact bytes.

record_index.caption: Record Index
record_index.description: One-based occurrence index of the record (line) within the artifact. This is the occurrence identity; native ids may repeat or be absent.

native_uid.caption: Native Record ID
native_uid.description: The record's own identifier when the source reports one.

native_time.caption: Native Time Text
native_time.description: The record's timestamp text verbatim, when reported.

record_bytes.caption: Record Bytes
record_bytes.description: Byte length of the record line excluding the line terminator.

record_type.caption: Record Type
record_type.description: The native record discriminator (for example type/subtype or event name) as the mapping contract defines it.

parse_status_id.caption: Parse Status ID
parse_status_id.description: Whether the retained record could be parsed as one JSON object.

2.caption: Malformed JSON
2.description: Decodable text that is not one JSON object (including duplicate keys under strict parsing).

3.caption: Undecodable bytes
3.description: The line is not valid UTF-8; raw_bytes_b64 holds the bytes.

4.caption: Blank
4.description: An empty line, retained to preserve framing.

5.caption: Incomplete at source end
5.description: The source ended (EOF or interruption) without a line terminator while the record was not yet one JSON object; the bytes received are retained verbatim.

raw_bytes_b64.caption: Raw Bytes (base64)
raw_bytes_b64.description: The exact bytes of a record that cannot be represented as a JSON string.

line_ending.caption: Line Ending
line_ending.description: The line terminator observed after the record: LF, CRLF or none (last line without terminator).

contract_uid.caption: Mapping Contract ID
contract_uid.description: Identifier of the mapping contract that produced this event, resolved through run.json.

contract_sha256.caption: Mapping Contract SHA-256
contract_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the mapping contract document embedded in run.json.

capture_time.caption: Capture Time
capture_time.description: When Journal observed or transformed the record, as epoch milliseconds.

capture_time_text.caption: Capture Time Text
capture_time_text.description: Journal's capture/transformation time at full precision, RFC 3339.

producer.caption: Producer
producer.description: The Journal producer (transformer) that wrote the event; distinct from the originating CLI in metadata.product.

tool_operation.caption: Operation
tool_operation.description: A separately reported operation executed within a tool call (for example one command of a multi-command exec).

is_whole_record.caption: Is Whole Record
is_whole_record.description: True when the event's data attribute holds the complete native record; false when it holds a fragment (for example one block). Reconstruction uses whole-record events only.

reported_decision.caption: Reported Decision
reported_decision.description: The source's own decision label exactly as reported (for example accept, denied). decision carries the normalized caption.

method_id.caption: Attribution Method ID
method_id.description: How the candidate owners of an attribution were obtained: from an identifier the source record itself reports at the declared path, or by a declared derivation rule (for example text containment within a scope). A derived association is never a reported parent identifier.

1.caption: Reported identifier
1.description: The source record names the owner at the declared path.

2.caption: Derived by rule
2.description: Candidates were computed by the declared rule named in basis; the source reports no owner identifier.

settings.caption: Session Settings
settings.description: Normalized launch/session settings reported by a native record, as a session_settings object. Only fields the record reports are present.

permission_mode.caption: Permission Mode
permission_mode.description: The CLI's reported permission/approval mode string exactly as reported (for example default, acceptEdits).

approval_policy.caption: Approval Policy
approval_policy.description: The CLI's reported approval policy string exactly as reported (for example never, on-request).

sandbox_policy.caption: Sandbox Policy
sandbox_policy.description: The CLI's reported sandbox policy exactly as reported (string or object).

tool_names.caption: Tool Names
tool_names.description: The tool names the CLI reported as available, in reported order.

git_branch.caption: Git Branch
git_branch.description: The git branch the CLI reported for the working directory.

context_kind.caption: Context Kind
context_kind.description: The native kind of a settings, injected-context or accounting record exactly as the source names it (for example init, environment, skill_listing, session_meta, turn_context, cost-state, token_usage_record).

rendered_role.caption: Rendered Role
rendered_role.description: The message role under which injected context was rendered to the model, when the source reports it.

rule_uid.caption: Mapping Rule ID
rule_uid.description: The rule of the mapping contract (contract_uid) that produced this event. Journal mapping provenance, declared here rather than in OCSF unmapped, which holds unmapped source data. Added in 0.5.0-prototype; earlier packages carry it as unmapped.rule_id.

command_line.caption: Command Line
command_line.description: The command exactly as the source reported it, as one string. Never parsed into argv; a shell's interpretation of it is not reported by this attribute.

identity_basis_id.caption: Identity Basis ID
identity_basis_id.description: What kind of identifier the source reported as this fact's identity: tool_call_uid on a tool_call event, uid on an operation, item_uid on a model_response. A stream-local item identifier is not the identifier the model used for the call or the provider's response identifier, and cannot be joined with one.

1.caption: Model-facing call identifier
1.description: The identifier the model's own tool request carried, as the source reports it.

2.caption: Stream-local item identifier
2.description: An identifier the CLI's output stream assigns to its own items. It is unique only within one source artifact of one Journal invocation (journal.run_uid, journal.invocation_index, source_ref.artifact): an equal value in another invocation is another item. The model-facing call or response identifier is not reported.

tool_namespace.caption: Tool Namespace
tool_namespace.description: The namespace the source reports beside the tool name, such as the MCP server of an MCP tool. Absent when the source reports none; never derived from the tool name.

measurement_status_id.caption: Measurement Status ID
measurement_status_id.description: What the source establishes about the reported quantity: of the whole usage observation, or (on a usage component) of that one component's canonical quantity. Separate from how Journal obtained a component (component_basis_id). Absent when no declared rule states it.

1.caption: Measured
1.description: The source establishes this exact value as a measurement of the quantity; for a running total, of every contribution to it.

2.caption: Possibly default
2.description: The source emits exactly these values also when it has no measurement (for example all-zero defaults); a measured value is not established.

3.caption: Conditional
3.description: On a usage component whose canonical value the source does not establish: a declared formula gives a result from the reported operands that is the component's quantity only under assumptions the component's derivation names (for example that a possibly default operand, or one that is only a lower bound, is a complete measurement). The result is the component's conditional_value, never the canonical value, which stays absent. A price estimate from it holds only under the same assumptions. Equal prices for the tranches between which the uncertain quantity could fall make that allocation immaterial to their subtotal; they do not make the subtotal exact when an operand is itself a lower bound, because no price recovers a contribution the source never reported.

4.caption: Lower bound
4.description: The quantity is at least this value, and that it equals the quantity is not established: the value sums measured contributions while a contribution the source did not receive, or for which it wrote its default, is missing (for example a running total that adds only the responses whose usage arrived and writes 0 for an omitted member). A positive running total therefore does not establish that every contribution was reported: a reported 100 is compatible with an actual 150. The value is kept as reported, never raised to a guessed quantity, and a price estimate computed from it is itself only a lower bound of the charge.

conditional_value.caption: Conditional Value
conditional_value.description: The result of a usage component's declared formula when the source does not establish the component's canonical value and the formula gives that quantity only under assumptions the component's derivation names (measurement_status_id 3 Conditional). Not the canonical value, which stays absent; consumers that use it inherit the named assumptions, and when an operand is a lower bound the result is no more complete than that operand.

reasoning_form_id.caption: Reasoning Form ID
reasoning_form_id.description: What a reasoning content block holds, as a declared rule establishes it from the source. Absent when the source does not establish it.

1.caption: Full reasoning
1.description: The model's reasoning text as produced.

2.caption: Summary
2.description: A summary of the model's reasoning, not its full text.

3.caption: Redacted
3.description: The source reports that reasoning occurred but withholds its text (for example encrypted or redacted reasoning).

text_update_id.caption: Text Update ID
text_update_id.description: How this block's text relates to the text of the same content item (item_uid) or response (response_uid) that earlier events of the same source artifact reported, as a declared rule establishes it. Absent when no rule states it; a consumer then assumes neither.

1.caption: Increment
1.description: The text continues the item's text: the item's text is the concatenation, in journal.sequence order, of the texts of its Increment blocks. An increment is not by itself asserted to be the whole text, and the assembled text is never concatenated with a whole text reported elsewhere (for example a turn's own response).

2.caption: Snapshot
2.description: The text is the item's whole text as of this record: it replaces any earlier view of the item and is never concatenated with one.

uncached_input_tokens.caption: Uncached Input Tokens
uncached_input_tokens.description: Ordinary input tokens: input neither read from nor written to a prompt cache. Disjoint from cache_read_tokens and cache_write_tokens. Present only when the source reports this component or a declared rule derives it exactly from components whose arithmetic the source establishes (components[] names which); otherwise absent and, when the source's components cannot establish it, listed as unavailable. A formula result that is this quantity only under named assumptions is never this value; it is the component's conditional_value. Replaces input_tokens of 0.5.0-prototype and earlier, whose meaning followed each vendor.

cache_write_tiers.caption: Cache Write Tiers
cache_write_tiers.description: The source-reported breakdown of cache_write_tokens by retention or pricing tier. Each tier's count is a part of cache_write_tokens, never additional usage.

tier.caption: Tier
tier.description: A tier exactly as the source names it (for example the member ephemeral_1h_input_tokens of Claude's cache_creation).

aggregation_id.caption: Aggregation ID
aggregation_id.description: How the observation's components accumulate, independently of its scope (scope_id) and finality (usage_status_id).

1.caption: Scope total
1.description: The consumption of exactly the observation's scope unit (for example one model response); observations of distinct units of that scope are disjoint.

2.caption: Cumulative snapshot
2.description: A running total of the scope unit from its start up to the point of observation. It may include consumption before this capture began and is not the unit's completed total; two snapshots of one unit overlap and are never summed.

3.caption: Single response
3.description: The consumption of one model response within the observation's scope unit, which the source may leave unidentified (for example the usage of a child run's last response that the spawning call's result reports): neither the unit's total nor a running total of it. It is never summed with the unit's other observations, and it is the same quantity as another observation only when both name the same response.

reasoning_relation_id.caption: Reasoning Relation ID
reasoning_relation_id.description: Whether reasoning_tokens are part of output_tokens, as the source's own arithmetic establishes. Absent when no declared rule establishes it.

1.caption: Part of output
1.description: reasoning_tokens are a subset of output_tokens: never another additive count or charge.

2.caption: Separate from output
2.description: reasoning_tokens are not counted in output_tokens.

components.caption: Components
components.description: For each canonical usage component this observation states or cannot state: whether its value was copied from a reported native member, derived by a declared rule from named native members, or is unavailable from what the source reported. The native values themselves stay in data.

component_basis_id.caption: Component Basis ID
component_basis_id.description: How a canonical usage component was established.

1.caption: Reported
1.description: Copied exactly from the one native member named.

2.caption: Derived
2.description: Computed exactly from the native members named, by the declared rule in derivation, whose arithmetic the source establishes.

3.caption: Unavailable
3.description: The source reports related members, but they do not establish this component (derivation states why); the component is absent, never zero.

native_pointers.caption: Native Pointers
native_pointers.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointers into the observation's data naming the native members a value was copied or derived from.

item_uid.caption: Item ID
item_uid.description: The source's own identifier of the content item an event observes (for example a Codex exec item id), unique only within the namespace identity_basis_id states. Not a model response identifier: one item is not one model invocation.

tool_family.caption: Tool Family
tool_family.description: The source's own family or item type of a tool activity, exactly as reported (for example the Codex exec item types mcp_tool_call, web_search, collab_tool_call and file_change). Not a tool name.

mcp.caption: MCP Observation
mcp.description: What this event observed of a Model Context Protocol interaction: protocol revision and basis, the addressed server and tool with their bases, and typed protocol objects (complete, partial CLI projection or schema example).

protocol_revision.caption: Protocol Revision
protocol_revision.description: The MCP protocol revision (for example 2025-11-25) only where the protocol exchange or a CLI artifact established it; never inferred from a CLI or SDK version.

1.caption: Reported in the protocol exchange
1.description: The negotiated revision of an acquired protocol message (for example an initialize result).

2.caption: Reported by a CLI artifact
2.description: A log or record the CLI wrote reports the negotiated revision for this session.

3.caption: Declared by the capture configuration
3.description: The capture declared it; not observed.

protocol_revision_basis.caption: Protocol Revision Basis
protocol_revision_basis.description: The caption of protocol_revision_basis_id, or the source's own basis for 99 Other.

target_server_name.caption: Target Server Name
target_server_name.description: The MCP server a call addresses, exactly as the source names it (usually the configured server key, which need not equal the server's self-reported name), independently of the call's reported tool_name.

1.caption: Reported members of the call
1.description: The call record names the server in a member of its own (for example server, mcpServerName).

2.caption: Reported dispatcher arguments
2.description: A dispatcher tool's reported arguments name it (for example call_mcp_tool ServerName).

3.caption: Declared derivation from an encoded tool name
3.description: Derived from the reported tool name by a pinned naming convention and confirmed unambiguous by the registered servers the source reported.

target_server_basis.caption: Target Server Basis
target_server_basis.description: The caption of target_server_basis_id, or the source's own basis for 99 Other.

target_tool_name.caption: Target Tool Name
target_tool_name.description: The MCP tool name on the addressed server, exactly as the source reports or the declared derivation yields it. The call's own tool_name and arguments are never rewritten to it.

3.caption: Declared derivation from an encoded tool name

target_tool_basis.caption: Target Tool Basis
target_tool_basis.description: The caption of target_tool_basis_id, or the source's own basis for 99 Other.

target_arguments_pointer.caption: Target Arguments Pointer
target_arguments_pointer.description: An RFC 6901 pointer into the event's own arguments locating the arguments the addressed tool receives (empty string: the arguments themselves; /Arguments inside a dispatcher envelope). Present only when such arguments are reported; nothing is copied.

protocol_objects.caption: Protocol Objects
protocol_objects.description: MCP protocol objects the source reported for this observation, each typed by the pinned binding.

protocol_definition.caption: Protocol Definition
protocol_definition.description: The official MCP definition name (for example CallToolResult) the protocol object is typed as.

binding_revision.caption: Binding Revision
binding_revision.description: The pinned MCP schema revision whose binding typed the protocol object. It is the binding used, not a claim about the negotiated revision (that is protocol_revision).

projection_id.caption: Projection ID
projection_id.description: Whether a protocol object is a complete acquired protocol object, a partial projection a CLI reported, or a labelled schema example.

1.caption: Complete protocol object
1.description: The object as the protocol carried it, acquired whole.

2.caption: Partial projection
2.description: Members a CLI reported in its own records, mapped to the protocol definition; members it did not report are absent and the required ones are listed in missing_required. Nothing is synthesized to complete it.

3.caption: Schema example
3.description: A labelled synthetic or official schema example, not an observation of a run.

projection_basis.caption: Projection Basis
projection_basis.description: Which source members were mapped to which protocol members, including any renaming the CLI applied (for example structured_content as structuredContent).

missing_required.caption: Missing Required Members
missing_required.description: Protocol-required members of the definition that a partial projection does not carry.

tool_definitions.caption: Tool Definitions
tool_definitions.description: Tools the source declared as available, each in its reported declaration format.

tool_description.caption: Tool Description
tool_description.description: A tool's description exactly as declared.

input_schema.caption: Input Schema
input_schema.description: The JSON Schema a tool declares for its input, exactly as reported.

output_schema.caption: Output Schema
output_schema.description: The JSON Schema a tool declares for its structured output, exactly as reported.

definition_format_id.caption: Definition Format ID
definition_format_id.description: The declaration format of a tool definition.

1.caption: MCP Tool
1.description: An MCP Tool definition (typed in mcp).

2.caption: Function declaration
2.description: A function-calling declaration (type function, name, description, parameters), as OpenAI-compatible APIs and OTel gen_ai.tool.definitions carry it.

3.caption: Name and schema hash
3.description: Only the tool name and a hash of its schema; the schema itself is not reported.

schema_hash.caption: Schema Hash
schema_hash.description: A hash of a tool's schema exactly as the source reported it; it identifies, it does not contain, the schema.

schema_dialect.caption: Schema Dialect
schema_dialect.description: The JSON Schema dialect URI the document or the source states ($schema); absent when neither states one.

schema_document.caption: Schema Document
schema_document.description: The JSON Schema document exactly as reported.

1.caption: JSON-RPC protocol error
1.description: An MCP or JSON-RPC error response (code, message, data).

2.caption: Tool result error
2.description: A tool result that reports an error as its content (MCP isError true).

3.caption: CLI-reported tool failure
3.description: The CLI reports that a tool call failed, without establishing which protocol layer failed.

4.caption: CLI or process failure
4.description: The CLI or its process reports a failure outside a tool call.

5.caption: Capture failure
5.description: Journal's own acquisition or persistence failed; not a vendor report.

error_code.caption: Error Code
error_code.description: An error code exactly as reported, keeping its JSON type (a JSON-RPC integer, a CLI string).

errors.caption: Errors
errors.description: Reported errors, each with its layer.

quantity_kind_id.caption: Quantity Kind ID
quantity_kind_id.description: What a cost observation counts. Different kinds are never added together, and only a Monetary amount has a currency.

1.caption: Monetary amount
1.description: Money in the stated currency.

2.caption: Premium requests
2.description: A count of premium requests the CLI reports as consumed.

3.caption: Model cost multiplier
3.description: A per-call model multiplier, or a sum of such multipliers, that a vendor reports for billing; not money and not a request count.

4.caption: Nano-AIU
4.description: Nano AI units a vendor reports.

quantity_kind.caption: Quantity Kind
quantity_kind.description: The caption of quantity_kind_id, or the source's own name for 99 Other.

quantity_unit.caption: Quantity Unit
quantity_unit.description: The unit a non-monetary billing quantity is stated in, as the source names it.

cost_observations.caption: Cost Observations
cost_observations.description: Every cost or billing quantity the record reports, each with its quantity kind, scope and aggregation. cost_observation keeps a single reported monetary total where routes reported one before 0.11.0.

assembly.caption: Assembly
assembly.description: How final assembly placed this event: canonical from one source, consolidated from several sources' observations, or a supporting observation that is evidence only.

assembly_role_id.caption: Assembly Role ID
assembly_role_id.description: The event's role in an assembled file. Canonical consumers read roles 1 and 3; role 2 is evidence and never counted as an execution.

1.caption: Canonical single observation
1.description: The only observation of its entity and stage among the declared sources.

2.caption: Supporting observation
2.description: One source's observation of an entity whose consolidated canonical event is in the same file.

3.caption: Consolidated canonical
3.description: The canonical event of an entity and stage that several sources observed, built from their compatible fields with per-field evidence.

entity_uid.caption: Entity ID
entity_uid.description: The logical entity and lifecycle stage in its declared identity namespace (for example tool_call/started/copilot.toolCallId:call_1).

occurrence_uid.caption: Occurrence ID
occurrence_uid.description: A source occurrence: artifact, one-based record index and the emit ordinal of the event within that record (artifact#record/ordinal).

relation_class_id.caption: Relation Class ID
relation_class_id.description: How the observations of one entity, or of one field, relate.

2.caption: Representation only
2.description: Equal values spelled differently (1 and 1.0).

3.caption: One richer
3.description: One observation carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

4.caption: Each richer
4.description: Each carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

5.caption: Conflicting
5.description: Two observations report different values for one field.

6.caption: Ambiguous
6.description: The identity repeats within one source, so no pairing is established.

7.caption: Single source
7.description: Only one observation reports the field.

8.caption: Superseded
8.description: A provisional observation of a quantity that a final observation of the same quantity (same scope, aggregation and model) supersedes: the canonical event carries the final one and the provisional one stays on its supporting observation, never counted again.

observation_refs.caption: Observation References
observation_refs.description: The source occurrences a consolidated event was built from.

emit_ordinal.caption: Emit Ordinal
emit_ordinal.description: The zero-based position of an event among the events its mapper emitted for one native record.

field_evidence.caption: Field Evidence
field_evidence.description: Per-field evidence of a consolidated event for every field whose observations are not identical.

field_pointer.caption: Field Pointer
field_pointer.description: An RFC 6901 pointer into the consolidated event.

occurrence_uids.caption: Occurrence IDs
occurrence_uids.description: The occurrences that reported a field.

selection_basis.caption: Selection Basis
selection_basis.description: Why the canonical value of a field is the one shown (single source, equal reports, a declared authority).

assembly_conflicts.caption: Assembly Conflicts
assembly_conflicts.description: Fields whose observations disagree, each value with its occurrence.

observed_values.caption: Observed Values
observed_values.description: Each disagreeing value with its occurrence: [{occurrence_uid, value}].

resolution.caption: Resolution
resolution.description: unresolved, or the declared authority that selected the canonical value.

execution_metrics.caption: Execution Metrics
execution_metrics.description: Source-reported non-token execution quantities. Each occurrence keeps its source metric name, native unit, scope and exact numeric value. These are separate observations, never totals of one another.

reported_value.caption: Reported Value
reported_value.description: The exact numeric value reported by the source, with no rounding or inference that a zero is a measured zero.

metric_name.caption: Metric Name
metric_name.description: The source-qualified metric name. Matching names alone do not establish equal windows or additive quantities.

metric_unit.caption: Metric Unit
metric_unit.description: The native quantity unit: ms, s, count or another explicitly named source unit.

file_changes.caption: File Changes
file_changes.description: Files the source reports as changed by this operation, at the observed lifecycle stage. A reported change is not an independently verified filesystem effect.

file_path.caption: File Path
file_path.description: The path exactly as the source reported it; no resolution against a guessed working directory.

change_kind.caption: Change Kind
change_kind.description: The native file-change kind exactly as reported.

element_index.caption: Element Index
element_index.description: Zero-based position in the source collection. Preserves multiplicity within this source occurrence; never a cross-source identity.

plan_items.caption: Plan Items
plan_items.description: The ordered plan items and completion flags exactly as the source reports them. Each snapshot is retained separately.

reported_completed.caption: Reported Completed
reported_completed.description: Whether the source marks this item complete; absence is not false.

task_uid.caption: Task Uid
task_uid.description: The task tracker identifier reported by the source; not a tool call, response or session identifier.

sender_session_uid.caption: Sender Session Uid
sender_session_uid.description: The sending session identifier explicitly reported by a collaboration tool observation.

recipient_session_uids.caption: Recipient Session Uids
recipient_session_uids.description: The receiving session identifiers explicitly reported by a collaboration tool observation. They do not establish spawned child runs or acquired child recordings.

agent_states.caption: Agent States
agent_states.description: Reported states of explicitly identified collaborating sessions.

configuration_source.caption: Configuration Source
configuration_source.description: The configuration origin exactly as the source reports it.

reasoning_effort.caption: Reasoning Effort
reasoning_effort.description: The configured reasoning-effort label exactly as the source reports it; no numeric scale is inferred.

task_description.caption: Task Description
task_description.description: The task tracker description exactly as reported.

agent_type.caption: Agent Type
agent_type.description: The task tracker agent type exactly as reported; not a model name.

agent_uid.caption: Agent ID
agent_uid.description: The native identifier of the child agent whose state or accounting is reported. No session identity is inferred.

server_connections.caption: Server Connections
server_connections.description: Configured MCP server connections and their reported state; no inferred protocol capabilities.

reported_agent.caption: Reported Agent
reported_agent.description: Source-reported agent identity and kind, without inferring a child relationship.

kind.caption: Reported Kind
kind.description: The exact source kind of this identity; it is not a Journal classification.

concept.caption: Quantity Concept
concept.description: Stable common concept of the quantity, as defined in execution_metric. Absence means a source-specific metric; metric_name is provenance, never the common concept.

measurement_window.caption: Measurement Window
measurement_window.description: The interval or snapshot the quantity concerns, independently of its subject. Defined in execution_metric; no summability follows.

cost_basis_window.caption: Pricing Basis Window
cost_basis_window.description: The interval to which cost_basis applies, independently of the amount aggregation: most_recent_request means the model pricing table for only its most recent request, never the cumulative history or an invoice.

combined_output.caption: Combined Output
combined_output.description: Combined command output exactly as the source reports it; the source does not establish separate standard output and standard error streams.

extension.json.caption: Agentic CLI
extension.json.name: agentic_cli
extension.json.description: Agent Journal's Agentic CLI extension prototype. Uses ACP's session, prompt turn, content block, tool call and permission vocabulary within OCSF. The uid 901 is a PROVISIONAL, UNREGISTERED prototype assignment: it is not reserved in the OCSF extensions registry and must not be used for a release package. Packages written against it pin this uid, this version and the compiled schema hash in run.json; readers resolve class names through that pin and refuse a mismatched assignment. Version 0.2.0-prototype moves invariant per-run facts (cli_agent, producer, capture time, contract and artifact hashes) to run.json: events reference them through journal.run_uid, journal.contract_uid and source_ref.artifact. attribution.method_id states whether candidates came from a source-reported identifier or a declared derivation rule. Version 0.3.0-prototype adds the session_context class (settings reported, context injected, accounting reported), the session_settings object, the Turn started activity of prompt_turn, the Incomplete-at-source-end parse status for a record cut off by the end of its source, and the settings/context attributes those use. Packages written incrementally by the Java writer pin this version. Version 0.4.0-prototype (FND-1, Owner decision 2026-10-22) makes cli_agent this extension's own object: it no longer extends the core ai_agent (no inherited ai_model, charter, uid_numeric or framework type enum); it declares name, version, uid, instance_uid and product. Version 0.5.0-prototype (SEM-1 candidate, 2026-10-22; its new meanings await the Project Owner's semantic approval) records the mapping rule as journal.rule_uid instead of in OCSF unmapped; adds identity_basis_id on tool_call and operation (a stream-local item identifier is not a model-facing call identifier), tool_namespace (for example an MCP server), command_line on operation (the reported command string, never parsed into argv), measurement_status_id on usage_observation (measured versus possibly the source's default) and reasoning_form_id on content_block (full reasoning versus a summary); an operation may be a standalone observation without a wrapping tool call. Version 0.6.0-prototype (SEM-CLOSE, the delegated semantic decisions of 2026-10-22; its changed meanings await the managing reviewer's binding) exposes usage in disjoint economic tranches: uncached_input_tokens replaces input_tokens (whose meaning followed each vendor), cache reads and writes are disjoint, cache_write_tiers breaks writes down, reasoning_relation_id states whether reasoning is part of output, aggregation_id (scope total or cumulative snapshot) is a facet beside scope and finality, and components[] states per component whether it was reported, derived by a declared rule or is unavailable. model_response.response_uid is optional and is only the provider's response identifier; a source-local content item is item_uid with its identity_basis_id, and activity 3 Item completed observes it without naming a response. tool_call gains activity 4 Started (an invocation the source reports as started, not the model's request) and tool_family (the source's item type, not a tool name). reasoning_form_id gains 3 Redacted. Version 0.7.0-prototype (Tier 1 foundation wave, 2026-10-22; candidate for the managing reviewer) adds measurement_status_id on usage_component: what the source establishes about each component's quantity (Measured, Possibly default, or 3 Conditional for a component derived from a possibly default operand), apart from how Journal obtained it; a Codex zero that the pinned emitter also writes when the provider omits the member is Possibly default even inside non-zero usage. Version 0.8.0-prototype (requirements consistency, 2026-10-23; candidate for the managing reviewer) rejects the assumption that a positive cumulative value establishes every contribution: measurement_status_id gains 4 Lower bound (at least this value; equality not established), and a formula result that holds only under named assumptions is the component's new conditional_value with status 3 Conditional, never the canonical value, which stays absent. Version 0.9.0-prototype (review closure, 2026-10-23; candidate for the managing reviewer) restates two descriptions without changing any attribute, enum value or shape: 4 Lower bound reads in the stated direction (the quantity is at least the value and may exceed it; a reported 100 is compatible with an actual 150; an estimate from it is only a lower bound of the charge), and 3 Conditional no longer suggests that equal prices make an estimate exact: they make the allocation between tranches immaterial to a subtotal, never recover a missing contribution. Version 0.10.0-prototype (Antigravity close-out, 2026-10-23; candidate for the managing reviewer) adds 99 Other to scope_id, whose sibling scope names a unit the source defines (for example Conversation step) and whose unit is the enclosing event's own item, so a finer source unit is never stated as a model response; and text_update_id on content_block, which states whether a block's text is an Increment of its item's text (concatenated in order) or a Snapshot that replaces earlier views, so assembling partial text needs no vendor knowledge. Version 0.11.0-prototype (Level 1 assembly and first-class MCP, 2026-10-24; candidate for review) contains the pinned MCP protocol data model: every object, union and typed map of the official 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 JSON Schemas is a generated mcp_* object (objects/mcp/, from journal-ocsf-writer McpBindingGenerator and the binding table that embeds and extracts them), reached through tool_call.mcp and session_context.mcp (mcp_observation: protocol revision with its basis, the addressed server and tool each with its own basis apart from the reported name and arguments, and protocol_objects typed by definition and labelled complete, partial CLI projection or schema example, with the required members a projection lacks). Shared objects carry what is common across vendors and protocols: tool_definition and json_schema for declared tools, error_info with the reporting layer (JSON-RPC, tool result, CLI, process, capture) on tool_result.errors, and cost_observation quantity kinds and units so that premium requests, model cost multipliers, nano-AIU and money stay distinct (currency is now required only of money). Final assembly is recorded per event in assembly (canonical from one source, consolidated with per-field evidence and conflicts, or a supporting observation that is evidence only). session_context gains activity 4 Outcome reported (the CLI's own exit code or lifecycle state), and source_kind_id gains 3 Telemetry export, 4 CLI report file and 5 CLI log file for the further sources a final assembly declares. Final assembly: every event may carry assembly (assembly_record: role, entity, occurrence, relation, observation references, field evidence, conflicts); relation_class_id gains 8 Superseded (a provisional observation a final one of the same quantity supersedes); cost_observation gains model_ref (a per-model quantity). Version 0.12.0-prototype (D1 canonical determinism, 2026-10-24; candidate for review) gives scope 7 Child run a unit: session_context gains tool_call_uid, the tool call whose spawned child run an accounting record reports, so child-run usage reported by the parent's records (Claude Code's Agent result and task progress/notification) is queryable at that child without being added to any parent total. Version 0.13.0-prototype (R1 ratchet review, 2026-10-24; candidate for review) separates ownership from the measurement window: aggregation_id gains 3 Single response, the consumption of one model response within the scope unit that the source may leave unidentified, neither the unit's total nor a running total, so a child run's last-response usage reported with the spawning call's result is never read as the child run's consumption. Version 0.16.0-prototype separates source-reported combined operation output from separately reported stdout/stderr, and preserves the source namespace of declared tools.

The layers stay distinct; an absent error is not a success and an absent isError is not false.
objects/error_info.json.name: error_info

message.description: The error message exactly as reported.

objects/execution_metric.json.caption: Execution Metric
objects/execution_metric.json.description: A source-reported execution quantity. Exact native value/unit, scope and source pointer are retained. Unknown measurement semantics stay Unknown; no sum or cross-source equivalence follows. Common concepts: model.context_capacity and model.output_limit are reported model configuration limits in tokens, never consumption; context.token_capacity, context.tokens_used and context.percent_used concern the observed context. duration.api is reported API time, duration.elapsed wall time, duration.model_dispatch the dispatch duration. latency.first_token, first_output_token, first_stream_frame, first_content_frame, request_dispatch and inter_token retain their distinct endpoints. model.request_count, execution.turn_count, user.request_count, tool.invocation_count, tool.available_count and server.web_search_count/web_fetch_count count their named entities only. change.lines_added/lines_removed/files_changed count reported changes. request.body_size and request.wire_size are bytes before/on transport; cache.retention is seconds. usage.reported_input is an inclusive native input count (not an uncached tranche); usage.output is output tokens. Windows: configuration_snapshot and context_snapshot are states at the observation; patch is one reported patch; model_request one request; most_recent_request the latest request only; model_cumulative/session_cumulative/run_cumulative the reported cumulative extent of that subject; conversation_step one source-defined step; task_tracker_snapshot the tracker measure; child_result the child result reported extent; run_initial_response the initial-response timing within the run. Different windows and subjects must not be aggregated or compared as equal measurements. Source-specific counters without an established common concept retain their native name.
objects/execution_metric.json.name: execution_metric

data.description: Exact source dimensions and window for a source-named metric. No join or cross-source aggregation is inferred.

objects/field_evidence.json.caption: Field Evidence
objects/field_evidence.json.description: Which occurrences supplied one field of a consolidated event and how their reports relate: a single source, identical, differing only in representation, or conflicting (the value then absent unless a declared authority selected one).
objects/field_evidence.json.name: field_evidence

objects/file_change.json.caption: File Change
objects/file_change.json.description: One reported file change at its source position.
objects/file_change.json.name: file_change

objects/model_ref.json.caption: Model Reference

objects/model_ref.json.name: model_ref

name.description: The model identifier exactly as reported.

version.description: The model version string, only when the source reports one separately from the model name.

objects/observation_ref.json.caption: Observation Reference
objects/observation_ref.json.description: One source occurrence that supports a consolidated event, found in this file as a supporting observation.
objects/observation_ref.json.name: observation_ref

objects/operation.json.caption: Operation
objects/operation.json.description: A separately reported operation with its own identity and observed outcome. objects/operation.json.name: operation

data.description: The native operation record exactly as reported.

objects/permission_decision.json.caption: Permission Decision

objects/permission_decision.json.name: permission_decision

data.description: The native decision record exactly as reported.

objects/plan_item.json.caption: Plan Item
objects/plan_item.json.description: One item in the source's plan snapshot.
objects/plan_item.json.name: plan_item

objects/reported_agent.json.caption: Reported Agent
objects/reported_agent.json.name: reported_agent
objects/reported_agent.json.description: A native agent identity within its source artifact/run. uid and kind are reported; neither implies a child, parent, spawn or session identity.

objects/server_connection.json.caption: Server Connection
objects/server_connection.json.description: One configured MCP connection, without inferred protocol negotiation or capabilities.
objects/server_connection.json.name: server_connection

name.description: The MCP server name reported by the source configuration.

objects/session_settings.json.caption: Session Settings
objects/session_settings.json.description: Launch/session settings as one native record reports them. Every attribute is optional: only reported values are present; nothing is defaulted or inferred.
objects/session_settings.json.name: session_settings

working_directory.description: The working directory the CLI reported.

model.description: The model identifier the CLI reported as configured.

provider.description: The model provider the CLI reported (a reported string, not an inferred organization).

version.description: The CLI version the record itself reports.

objects/source_ref.json.caption: Source Reference
objects/source_ref.json.description: Identifies the native artifact and record occurrence that supplied a fact. The artifact hash is stored once per run in run.json sources and reached through artifact; it appears here only in a self-contained export.
objects/source_ref.json.name: source_ref

objects/tool_definition.json.caption: Tool Definition
objects/tool_definition.json.description: A tool the CLI or a server declared as available, in any declaration format (an MCP Tool, a function declaration, a vendor tool record): its name, description, input and output JSON Schemas and annotations as reported. objects/tool_definition.json.name: tool_definition

name.description: The tool name exactly as declared.

title.description: A human-readable title the declaration gives the tool, exactly as declared.

data.description: The native declaration exactly as reported.

objects/tool_result.json.caption: Tool Result
objects/tool_result.json.description: The result returned for a tool call as the source reported it.
objects/tool_result.json.name: tool_result

data.description: The model-visible result content exactly as reported (string, array or object).

errors.description: Each error reported for this result with the layer that reported it (JSON-RPC, tool result, CLI, capture).

objects/usage_component.json.caption: Usage Component
objects/usage_component.json.description: How one canonical usage component of an observation was established: reported (copied from one native member), derived exactly by a declared rule from named native members, or unavailable from what the source reported; and, where a declared rule establishes it, what the source establishes about the component's quantity (measured, possibly the source's default, at least the stated value, or, for an unavailable component, a conditional formula result kept apart from the canonical value).
objects/usage_component.json.name: usage_component

name.description: The canonical component attribute, for example uncached_input_tokens.

measurement_status_id.description: What the source establishes about this component's quantity, apart from component_basis_id; absent when no declared rule states it.

conditional_value.description: With measurement_status_id 3 Conditional: the declared formula's result, which is this component's quantity only under the assumptions the derivation names; the canonical component value stays absent.

derivation.description: The declared rule and its arithmetic for a derived component; for a conditional value, the formula and every assumption it needs; why the component is unavailable otherwise.

objects/usage_observation.json.caption: Usage Observation
objects/usage_observation.json.description: One reported token-usage observation, in disjoint economic tranches: uncached input, cache reads and cache writes (with their tiers), and output with its reasoning part. Scope, aggregation and finality are separate facets; components are present only when reported or exactly derived (components[] says which); absence is not zero. data keeps the native usage object exactly.
objects/usage_observation.json.name: usage_observation

scope_id.description: The scope at which the source reported this observation. At 99 Other the unit, named in scope, is the enclosing event's own item: its item_uid (or tool_call_uid) in the namespace that event's identity_basis_id states, within the observation's source artifact. declarations.question: How many user submissions did this run contain, and which native records represent each one?
declarations.identity: (run_uid, turn_uid, exact concatenated block text) when the record reports a turn id: records with the same key are representations of one submission. Without a turn id each occurrence stands alone (identity_basis occurrence); the view cannot tell a repeated representation from a new identical-text submission and says so. A record classified by a classifier below is not a submission.

classifiers.label: environment_context
classifiers.basis: Codex writes the environment context as a user-role message before the prompt; user role alone does not establish human authorship

declarations.question: How many model responses were there, and what did each one contain across all its native updates?
declarations.identity: (run_uid, response_uid) when identity_scope is run (the source reports a stable response id); (run_uid, artifact, response_uid) when identity_scope is artifact (ids are scoped to one artifact, for example Codex stream item ids). A missing response_uid is unresolved, never guessed.

update_semantics.basis: each stream record carries one further content block of the same message id; the Completed record ends the sequence
each transcript record carries one further content block of the same message id
item_completed AgentMessage and response_item message repeat the full message with one id; snapshots must agree
the exec stream reports completed content items (item_uid, stream-local), not response identities; which items belong to one model response is not reported, so no assembly is possible

the stream reports agent-response steps as content items (item_uid, the conversation's step index) whose text_delta fragments are Increment blocks of the step's text, never a response identity; which steps belong to one model response is not reported, so no response assembly is possible (items are assembled separately)

declarations.cross_source: when one identity has occurrences in several artifacts (live output and saved session file), each artifact is assembled separately and the assemblies are compared; a difference is reported, never reconciled
declarations.items: Separately from responses: model_response events that report an item_uid are grouped by (run_uid, artifact, item_uid); an item's text is assembled from its blocks' text_update_id alone: Increment texts concatenated in journal.sequence order, a Snapshot replacing the text so far; a text block without text_update_id leaves the item's assembly unavailable (the update mode is not stated). No vendor block type is read, and no text reported on another class (for example a prompt turn's own response) is added to an item.

declarations.question: Which reported usage figures are the applicable final values, at which scope, from which source, and how many repeated or provisional observations exist beside them?
declarations.rule: Group observations by (run_uid, scope_id, owner, model name, source artifact), where owner is response_uid at Model-response scope, turn_uid at Prompt-turn scope, session_uid at Session scope, run_uid at Run and Model scope, and at Other scope (99) the enclosing event's own item (item_uid, else tool_call_uid) within the source artifact, with the scope name (the unit the source defines, for example Conversation step) part of the group so that differently named units never share a group; an Other observation on an event without an item identity is unidentified, never pooled with another. Within a group the applicable final is the Final observations' component set when every Final observation reports equal components (repeats are counted once and listed); differing Final observations are a conflict with no applicable value; a group without a Final observation has none, and its Provisional/Unknown observations remain visible. Groups are never summed across scopes, sources, models or child runs; absence of a component is not zero. A finer source unit is not a model response: Other-scope groups are never counted as responses, and their totals are never added to a Session, Run or Model observation that covers them. Every observation also exposes component_evidence with its measurement status, conditional_value and premise; a conditional value is never an applicable canonical value.

declarations.question: Which facts are associated with which owner, by how many candidates, and on what evidence?
declarations.rule: Candidate count and evidence method are reported separately. method Reported identifier means the cited native record names the owner at the declared path; method Derived by rule means candidates were computed (for example command text contained in a call input within the same turn). A unique Derived candidate is a derived association, never a reported parent id. A decision whose outcome is Unattributed or Ambiguous stays at its reported scope and is never attached to a tool call.

declarations.question: Which result belongs to which tool request, including repeated or identical results?
declarations.rule: A result belongs to the tool_call_uid its own native record reports at the declared path (Claude content[].tool_use_id, Codex payload.call_id or the exec stream's item id, Antigravity step_index). An owner whose identity_basis_id is present and not 1 Model-facing call identifier (a stream-local item identifier, a conversation step index) is an owner only within its source artifact: an equal value in another artifact is another owner. Equal content never pairs a result with a request; identical results under different owners remain separate and are listed as such.

declarations.question: Which launch/session settings, injected context and session accounting did the sources report, at what scope, and from which record?
declarations.rule: Every session_context event is one row at its reported scope (session when turn_uid is absent, turn otherwise). Settings rows list exactly the settings fields the record reported; nothing is merged across records, so two records reporting the same field remain two rows and a disagreement is visible. Context rows carry the kind, the rendered role and the text length; accounting rows are listed with the usage/cost groups they contribute to the usage view. A permission decision is not a setting: it stays in the association view at its reported scope.

declarations.question: Which events of an assembled file are the canonical record of the execution, and which are source observations kept only as evidence?
declarations.rule: an event without assembly, or with assembly_role_id 1 (Canonical single observation) or 3 (Consolidated canonical), is canonical; assembly_role_id 2 (Supporting observation) is evidence for the consolidated event of the same entity_uid and is excluded from every count, assembly and selection the other operations make
declarations.basis: final assembly writes each source's observations and, for an entity several sources observed, one consolidated event with per-field evidence; counting both would count one execution twice

time_policy.time: source-reported time when the record has one (time_basis 1); else the latest preceding reported time in the same artifact, else capture start (time_basis 2); metadata.original_time holds the source text verbatim; ordering is journal.sequence, never time
